paper_memo.memo_title: CMR #12 — Sansha City in the South China Sea

sections.heading: 1. Context and core thesis
sections.body: Haver argues that the creation of Sansha turned an existing set of Chinese administrative claims into a municipal system designed to normalize governance of disputed areas.

sections.heading: 2. Argument and evidence by section
sections.body: The introduction separates State Council approval from inauguration. The historical section traces earlier administrative arrangements. The substantive chapters connect civil services, local institutions, economic policy, environmental administration, and rights-protection activities to a common administrative project. The conclusion interprets these activities as mutually reinforcing.

sections.heading: 3. Source, edition, and claim checks

Zoe Haver. China Maritime Report No. 12: Sansha City in China's South China Sea Strategy: Building a System of Administrative Control. China Maritime Studies Institute, U.S. Naval War College, January 2021. The supplied PDF begins with a repository citation sheet. The supplied file contains 57 PDF pages.

Records distinguish June 2012 approval, July inauguration, creation of two districts in April 2020, and opening of the municipal prosecution office. The jurisdictional language is treated as China’s domestic administrative claim. Repeated references to the 2012 notice, the June 2015 courtroom dispatch, and one 2020 recruitment announcement are grouped.

Additional checks cover the school, business registration, fisheries and corporate records, municipal finances, and the statutory chronology surrounding the city’s creation. Repeated uses of tax data, registration reporting, and inauguration coverage are grouped.

This review added 93 source rows. Citation locators identify the text indexed from the supplied PDF. Source findings distinguish publisher or official checks from originals still awaiting review.
